conversation: Hi everyone. My family taught me to fish here, and I want this lake to keep supporting our village for years to come. With 100 tons in the lake, we can each catch 10 tons this month, leave 50 to reproduce, and start next month back at 100. That’s $10,000 each every month if we stick together. Can we agree to that limit and review our catches together each month? John, what do you think?

I’m on board, Luke. My family has depended on this lake too, and a steady living for all five of us beats a big catch followed by empty nets. I’ll keep my catch to 10 tons and share my total at our monthly review. John, would that work for you?

Count me in for 10 tons. My family taught me to leave enough in the water for the next catch, and this gives all five families a steady income. If the lake ever starts a month below 100 tons, let’s lower our limits together so it can recover. Kate and Emma, are you both comfortable with that?

I’m comfortable with that—10 tons for me this month. Keeping this lake healthy means our families and the village can count on it, not just today but for years ahead. If stocks fall, let’s agree on reduced catches before anyone heads out. Kate, does that work for you too?

Yes, I’ll keep my catch to 10 tons too. That gives us a fair living while leaving enough fish for next month—the way my family taught me to look after this lake. We’re all agreed: 10 tons each this month, then compare catches and check the stock together before setting next month’s limits.
